findings.evidence: Basis/Basic.lean:167 `section Span` under `[Semiring R]`; Basis/Defs.lean:78 base `[Semiring R]` for `constr`; StrongRankCondition.lean:426 `omit [StrongRankCondition R]`, :445 `finrank_eq_nat_card_basis`; grep for `sub_|neg|AddCommGroup` in the PR file: no matches.
findings.fix: Replace `[CommRing k]` with `[CommSemiring k]` in all four locations (keeping `[Nontrivial k]` on `finrank_eq_natCard`) and confirm the file still compiles.
findings.issue: `[CommRing k]` is stronger than necessary throughout (declared at the `IsFactorSet` class and the `IsFactorSet`, `Translation`, and `Algebra` section `variable` lines). No proof uses subtraction/negation (grep for `sub_`/`neg`/`AddCommGroup` returns nothing), and all cited API works over a commutative semiring: `Basis.span`, `Basis.constr`, and `finrank_eq_nat_card_basis` require only `[Semiring R]`, and `Module.End k M`/`Submodule.toSubalgebra` need only `[CommSemiring k]`. The comparable object `MonoidAlgebra k G` — which this PR itself maps to via `monoidAlgebraEquiv` — is a `k`-algebra for `CommSemiring k`.

summary: The construction never uses additive inverses, yet requires `[CommRing k]`; the natural level is `[CommSemiring k]`, matching the analogous `MonoidAlgebra k G` (a `k`-algebra over any commutative semiring).
